problem: Large language models struggle to optimally integrate supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning into a single training pipeline.
approach: Introduces SRFT, a single-stage framework that unifies SFT and RL through entropy-aware weighting mechanisms, simultaneously applying both paradigms rather than sequential two-stage methods.
contribution: SRFT outperforms zero-RL baselines by 9.0% on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks and 10.9% on three out-of-distribution benchmarks while maintaining stable policy entropy.

problem: Image inpainting models lack alignment with human aesthetic preferences, and understanding how to effectively use preference data for training remains unclear.
approach: Leverages direct preference optimization with public reward models to construct preference training datasets, conducting systematic experiments across nine reward models and two baselines.
contribution: Demonstrates that reward model ensembles mitigate individual biases and significantly outperform prior models across standard metrics and human evaluations without structural changes.

problem: Accurate 3D pose and shape reconstruction for non-human primates lags behind other species, limiting behavioral analysis in ethology and neuroscience.
approach: Introduces BigMaQ, a large-scale dataset of 750+ scenes of interacting macaques with 3D skeletal joint rotations from 16 calibrated cameras and paired action labels.
contribution: Provides subject-specific textured avatars and a benchmark (BigMaQ500) linking surface-based pose vectors to frames across multiple individuals, advancing beyond sparse keypoint tracking.

problem: Firms building high-stakes decision systems face pressure to search for less discriminatory algorithms but lack formal criteria for determining when their search effort is sufficient.
approach: Formalizes the search for less discriminatory algorithms as an optimal stopping problem and proposes an adaptive stopping algorithm that provides high-probability upper bounds on achievable gains.
contribution: Enables developers to certify to courts or regulators that they have sufficiently explored the space of models with lower disparate impact.

problem: Identifying high-quality fine-tuning data that balances difficulty and diversity typically requires manual expertise, making it costly to select premium datasets from large corpora.
approach: Introduces Difficulty-Diversity Collaborative Filtering (DDCF), which uses a seed dataset to predict correctness across an unannotated corpus and automatically selects data tailored to each model's characteristics.
contribution: Reduces annotation cost by 100-200 times while maintaining downstream performance comparable to full-corpus fine-tuning.

problem: Training LLMs on multi-domain datasets with mismatched data volumes leads to imbalanced performance across different capabilities and domains.
approach: Proposes IDEAL, a gradient-based framework that iteratively refines training data distributions by dynamically adjusting domain-specific data volumes based on their impact on downstream task performance.
contribution: Achieves balanced dataset composition enabling models to maintain robust generalization and consistent proficiency across diverse tasks.

problem: Current sim-to-real robotic learning requires extensive human effort to engineer training curricula and rewards, limiting scalability for long-horizon dexterous manipulation tasks.
approach: Introduces OmniReset, a system that leverages diverse simulator resets for simplifying long-horizon exploration and automatically generates resets with minimal human input to scale with compute.
contribution: Solves complex dexterous manipulation tasks without auto-curricula or human demonstrations, and enables successful real-world transfer when augmented with small amounts of real-world data.

problem: Single-space diffusion models struggle to simultaneously capture multi-modal time series distributions while preserving local temporal fidelity.
approach: Proposes L2D-Diff, a dual-space diffusion framework that first compresses sequences into latent space to model representation distributions, then uses a data-space model to refine local details.
contribution: Achieves faithful generation of multi-modal time series distributions without external conditions on both single-modal and multi-modal datasets.

problem: Long video generation faces challenges in both efficiency and quality, with existing methods trading off between bidirectional attention quality and causal attention speed.
approach: Introduces LongLive, a frame-level autoregressive framework using causal attention with KV-recache, streaming prompt tuning, and frame-level attention sinks for real-time interactive generation.
contribution: Fine-tunes a 1.3B model for minute-long generation in 32 GPU-days and sustains 20.7 FPS on a single H100, achieving strong performance on VBench for both short and long videos.

problem: Existing Rademacher complexity bounds for neural networks apply to limited model types and do not explain why high-rank weight matrices generalize well.
approach: Derives a new Rademacher complexity bound using Koopman operators, group representations, and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces (RKHSs) to construct an algebraic representation framework.
contribution: Provides theoretical explanation for why high-rank neural networks generalize well and extends applicability to a wider range of realistic models.

problem: Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) suffers from unstable policy updates due to extreme importance-weighted rewards on individual tokens.
approach: Proposes Geometric-Mean Policy Optimization (GMPO), replacing GRPO's arithmetic mean with geometric mean of token-level rewards to reduce sensitivity to outliers.
contribution: GMPO-7B improves average Pass@1 over GRPO by up to 4.1% on multiple mathematical reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Existing angle testing methods in high-dimensional spaces rely on Gaussian random projections and require asymptotic assumptions about projection count.
approach: Proposes two projection-based probabilistic kernel functions using deterministic structure and reference angles for angle comparison and thresholding without asymptotic assumptions.
contribution: Achieves 2.5-3X higher query-per-second throughput compared to state-of-the-art graph-based search on approximate nearest neighbor search tasks.

problem: All-in-one image restoration methods either ignore degradation priors or suffer from errors in degradation estimation, resulting in performance gaps versus task-specific models.
approach: Introduces UniRestorer with hierarchical clustering on degradation space and multi-granularity mixture-of-experts that adaptively selects experts using both degradation and granularity estimation.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art all-in-one methods by large margins and approaches performance of specific single-task models.

problem: Current robotics research focuses primarily on control strategies while overlooking tool design as a complementary form of physical intelligence that could simplify manipulation tasks.
approach: Presents VLMgineer, which uses Vision-Language Models and evolutionary search to automatically design tools and actions from scratch for manipulation tasks.
contribution: Discovers tools and policies that solve tasks more effectively than human-crafted tools and successfully transfers automatically designed tools to real-world robot execution.

problem: Uncertainty estimation in deep learning typically addresses only one type of uncertainty and requires model retraining, limiting practical deployment in high-stakes domains.
approach: Introduces CUPID, a plug-in module that jointly estimates aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty through learned Bayesian mapping and structured perturbations without model modification.
contribution: Provides layer-wise uncertainty insights and competitive performance across classification, regression, and out-of-distribution detection tasks.

problem: Post-training quantization of LLMs to 4-bit precision suffers from severe accuracy degradation due to errors in both activation and weight saliency.
approach: Proposes SERQ, a saliency-aware error reconstruction method using a single low-rank compensation matrix with static activation flattening, saliency-aware reconstruction, and offline weight permutation.
contribution: Enables efficient 4-bit matrix multiplication while keeping latency overhead minimal through offline processing.

problem: Time series foundation models achieve strong predictive performance but their calibration properties remain unexplored despite being critical for practical deployment.
approach: Systematically evaluates calibration of five recent time series foundation models across varying prediction heads and long-term autoregressive forecasting settings.
contribution: Demonstrates that time series foundation models are consistently better calibrated than baseline models and tend not to be systematically over- or under-confident.

problem: Event cameras produce asynchronous sparse sequential data that challenges standard tensor-based machine learning approaches designed for dense synchronous inputs.
approach: Introduces EVA, an asynchronous-to-synchronous framework inspired by language modeling that adapts linear attention and self-supervised learning for event-by-event feature generation.
contribution: Achieves 47.7 mAP on Gen1 detection, representing the first A2S framework to successfully master demanding event-based detection tasks.

problem: Existing graph generative model evaluation metrics (MMD-based) lack absolute performance measures and are sensitive to arbitrary parameterization choices across different descriptors.
approach: Introduces PolyGraphScore (PGS), which approximates Jensen-Shannon distance by fitting binary classifiers to distinguish real from generated graphs, constrained to unit interval [0,1].
contribution: Provides more robust and comparable evaluation metrics across different graph descriptors with theoretically grounded summary scores.

problem: Model-driven compression requires exact matching of predictions between compressor and decompressor, but non-deterministic differences cause cascading decoding failures.
approach: Formalizes prediction mismatch and introduces Probability Matching Interval Coding (PMATIC), a model-agnostic algorithm tolerating bounded prediction mismatch with low overhead.
contribution: Maintains correctness while achieving compression rates outperforming standard modern compression tools even with prediction mismatch.

problem: Multimodal misinformation detection requires robust reasoning about social complexity but faces a trade-off between limited single-agent analysis and computationally expensive multi-agent methods.
approach: Proposes Multi-Social-Agent Self-Distillation framework that internalizes collective social reasoning by simulating diverse MLLM judgments and using Social Correction Value-Driven Preference Optimization.
contribution: A 7B Qwen2-VL model significantly outperforms MLLM baselines and competes with proprietary models like GPT-4o and Claude on MFC-Bench and MMFakeBench.

problem: Existing text-to-SQL benchmarks fail to reflect production-grade database systems requiring multi-turn interactions, error recovery, and full CRUD operations.
approach: Introduces BIRD-INTERACT with comprehensive interaction environment, hierarchical knowledge bases, function-driven user simulator, and two evaluation settings (conversational and agentic).
contribution: Provides realistic benchmark covering full CRUD spectrum with 600 tasks featuring ambiguous and follow-up sub-tasks requiring dynamic interaction.

problem: Federated multi-task learning typically assumes model homogeneity across users, limiting applicability in realistic settings with diverse models and tasks.
approach: Proposes FedMuscle with Muscle loss, a contrastive learning objective that aligns representations across all participating models by maximizing mutual information.
contribution: Handles both model and task heterogeneity while consistently outperforming state-of-the-art baselines on diverse image and language tasks.

problem: GRPO-based text-to-image alignment suffers from sparse reward problem where terminal rewards for entire denoising trajectories miss fine-grained step contributions.
approach: Introduces DenseGRPO which predicts step-wise reward gains as dense rewards via ODE-based approach and calibrates exploration space with reward-aware timestep-specific stochasticity.
contribution: Dense rewards enable effective training by aligning feedback signals with intermediate denoising step contributions across multiple standard benchmarks.

problem: KV cache eviction methods assume that important cache entries remain stable across generation, but this assumption is fragile in extreme cases causing quality degradation.
approach: Proposes DefensiveKV and Layer-DefensiveKV with defensive aggregation strategy that controls worst-case risk through two-step linear-time approach versus mean aggregation.
contribution: Reduces generation quality loss by 2.3 times and 4.3 times compared to strongest baselines under 20% cache size across 18 datasets.

problem: Existing LLM benchmarks focus on short-form question answering but real-world expert workflows demand long-form outputs exceeding 5,000 tokens with strict domain-specific requirements.
approach: Introduces ExpertLongBench with 11 expert-level tasks from 9 domains and proposes CLEAR, an evaluation framework deriving checklists from rubric-aligned extraction of outputs.
contribution: Shows top performer (Gemini-2.5-Pro) achieves only 33.4 F1 score, revealing significant room for improvement on expert-level tasks.

problem: Traditional penetration testing for web security is expensive and requires specialized expertise, while computer-use agents' cybersecurity capabilities on complex web applications remain unknown.
approach: Introduces HackWorld, an evaluation framework exposing computer-use agents to 36 curated applications with realistic vulnerabilities across multiple frameworks.
contribution: Reveals state-of-the-art computer-use agents exploit vulnerabilities at below 12% rates, struggling with multi-step attacks and security tool usage.

problem: Text-guided image editing requires understanding not just what to modify but what to preserve, yet existing models lack principled control mechanisms.
approach: Reveals guidance signal follows semantic hierarchy formalized as Semantic Scale Hypothesis grounded in Tweedie's formula, then introduces Prism-Edit for decomposing guidance into semantic layers.
contribution: Enables precise, robust, and controllable editing through training-free plug-and-play module with interpretable layer-wise control.

problem: Interpreting dynamic and multi-faceted value trade-offs in LLMs lacks formal tools despite their importance for alignment and behavior prediction.
approach: Uses cognitive models from speech politeness to systematically evaluate value trade-offs in reasoning models and RL post-training dynamics.
contribution: Demonstrates patterns of higher informational than social utility in reasoning models and reveals how training dynamics shift utility values in predictable ways.

problem: SGD optimization on infinite-dimensional quadratic problems with power law spectral conditions achieves suboptimal rates when noise is present.
approach: Identifies (S)GD algorithms with complex plane contours and shows corner structures with external angle theta-pi accelerate convergence by balancing noise amplification against acceleration.
contribution: Achieves optimal rates up to O(t^-2-zeta) through contour-based optimization while accounting for spectral and noise conditions.

problem: Existing image generation benchmarks lag behind proprietary model capabilities and fail to capture emerging use cases and complex creative tasks.
approach: Introduces ECHO, a framework constructing benchmarks from real-world evidence via social media posts showcasing novel prompts with user judgments.
contribution: Curates 35,000 prompts revealing complex tasks absent from existing benchmarks and surfaces community feedback for metric design.

problem: LLMs on text-attributed graphs struggle in few-shot semi-supervised settings due to difficulty generating reliable pseudo labels and noise from LLM fine-tuning.
approach: Proposes GNN-as-Judge framework leveraging structural inductive bias of GNNs to identify influential unlabeled nodes and exploit agreement/disagreement patterns for pseudo-labeling.
contribution: Significantly outperforms existing methods under low-resource regimes by combining collaborative pseudo-labeling with weakly-supervised LLM fine-tuning.

problem: Existing LLM alignment methods work with single preferences but real datasets contain conflicts from multiple fine-grained, aspect-specific preferences.
approach: Proposes data-centric approach formalizing direct fine-grained preference optimization and recasting conflicted optimization as data selection with preference divergence metric.
contribution: Using just 30% of data with lowest preference divergence achieves consistent improvement over standard full-data alignment across varied settings.

problem: Flow-based generative models achieve quality improvement through optimal transport coupling but existing OT methods suffer from curse of dimensionality and scalability limits.
approach: Introduces AlignFlow using Semi-Discrete Optimal Transport (SDOT) that partitions noise space into Laguerre cells mapped to data points for efficient alignment.
contribution: Bypasses curse of dimensionality and scales to large datasets as plug-and-play enhancement for multiple state-of-the-art FGM algorithms.

problem: Multimodal LLMs with tool augmentation rely on single atomic tools and lack ability to select effective tool combinations for complex multi-turn reasoning tasks.
approach: Introduces AdaReasoner framework teaching dynamic tool orchestration through data curation methodology and tailored Tool GRPO algorithm for multi-turn tool-calling optimization.
contribution: 7B models achieve substantial gains (+38.7% average) and near-perfect accuracy on Visual Spatial Planning (97.6%), surpassing GPT-5 and Claude Sonnet 4.

problem: Vision-Language models for radiology reports optimize for narrative coherence which weakens visual grounding and leads to factual inaccuracies in medical descriptions.
approach: Proposes LLaVA-TA that decomposes reports into independent clinically-relevant topics and trains models to generate findings conditioned on full image and anatomical regions.
contribution: Sets new state-of-art on MIMIC-CXR improving RadGraph F1 from 29.4 to 44.0 and CheXpert F1-14 from 39.5 to 71.5.

problem: GPU kernel optimization remains labor-intensive and manual despite LLMs showing potential, as existing approaches treat them as single-shot generators without exploring irregular design spaces.
approach: Introduces STARK, an LLM agentic framework using multi-agent collaboration, grounded instruction, dynamic context management, and strategic search to mimic expert engineer workflows.
contribution: Produces correct solutions where baselines fail and achieves up to 16X faster runtime performance on KernelBench.

problem: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback assumes single universal reward overlooking diverse user preferences and limiting personalization in aligned AI systems.
approach: Proposes Swap-guided Preference Learning (SPL) using fictitious swap annotators to guide encoder and mitigate posterior collapse in Variational Preference Learning.
contribution: Mitigates collapse, enriches user-specific latents, and improves preference prediction with three components including Preferential Inverse Autoregressive Flow.

problem: Video feature privacy preservation requires retraining entire utility models for each task and cannot handle frozen foundation models, making it unsuitable for modern video architectures.
approach: Introduces Anonymizing Adapter Module (AAM) that removes private information from video features via plug-and-play adapter with self-supervised privacy, co-training, and latent consistency objectives.
contribution: Achieves 35% reduction in privacy leakage while maintaining near-baseline utility across Action Recognition, Temporal Action Detection, and Anomaly Detection tasks.

problem: Enforcing exact symmetry in machine learning models for scientific applications limits flexibility despite approximate symmetry offering greater robustness.
approach: Introduces averaging complexity framework quantifying cost of enforcing symmetry and proves exponential separation: exact symmetry requires linear complexity while approximate achieves logarithmic.
contribution: Provides first theoretical separation formally justifying why approximate symmetry is preferable in practice for scientific machine learning.
